question: Should OpenClaw solve memory-wiki isolation through a generic agent-scoped plugin config contract, a memory-wiki-specific ctx-aware vault resolver, or a narrower documented unsupported state for shared-gateway multi-agent use?
rationale: The request changes configuration/API surface and sensitive memory isolation semantics, so automation cannot safely choose precedence, SecretRef, validation, lifecycle, and upgrade behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a shared agents.list[].plugins contract with explicit merge precedence, SecretRef handling, validation, restart semantics, doctor coverage, and memory-wiki tests/docs using that contract.

options.title: Add memory-wiki-owned vault routing
options.body: Keep plugin config global and add a memory-wiki-specific per-agent or ctx-aware vault resolver with fail-closed no-context behavior and docs for CLI/gateway limitations.

options.title: Defer first-class isolation
options.body: Document shared-gateway memory-wiki vault isolation as unsupported for now and point operators to separate gateway processes until the broader plugin config contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a shared agents.list[].plugins contract with explicit merge precedence, SecretRef handling, validation, restart semantics, doctor coverage, and memory-wiki tests/docs using that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans the plugin/config/security boundary where Peter has recent relevant history and is the strongest routing candidate from the likely-owner set.
